brief.headline: Global Tech Rout Deepens as Anthropic Slides; Nifty Faces Pressures Despite Bank Rally
brief.summary: Wall Street equities plummeted overnight with the Nasdaq sinking 5.28% as an AI selloff triggered a broader market correction. Domestic equities face global contagion risks despite yesterday's 1.12% gain in the Nifty 50 and strong banking performance. Macro pressures persist with India's forex reserves dropping and expectations building for RBI interest rate hikes.

takeaways.text: US tech stocks plunged into a bear market overnight as Nasdaq tumbled 5.28% and S&P 500 dropped 3.70% on intensifying AI spending concerns.
A Reuters poll indicates the RBI is expected to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and reach 6% in February.
Gold dropped to 3539.0, prompting sharp cuts and margin warnings across jewellery retailers and gold loan lenders including Titan, Muthoot, and Manappuram.
IndusInd Bank surged 8.5% to ₹1,001 on quarterly profitability, though management subsequently terminated ex-CEO Sumant Kathpalia's employment over misconduct.
Jefferies initiated bullish coverage on five Adani group stocks with up to 43% upside and projected a 20% rally for Ambuja Cements.
India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $14.21 billion to $705.34 billion for the week ended November 13.

sections.india: The Nifty 50 gained 1.12% to 25800.6 yesterday, buoyed by a 2.49% surge in Bank Nifty and an 8.5% rally in IndusInd Bank to ₹1,001. Macro conditions face tightening as a Reuters poll projects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and 6% in February. Weakness in gold to 3539.0 continues to weigh on jewellers and gold financiers, while forex reserves fell $14.21 billion to $705.34 billion.
sections.world: US equities closed sharply lower overnight, with the S&P 500 dropping 3.70% and the Dow Jones falling 1.93% into market correction territory. Federal Reserve officials Anna Paulson and Lisa Cook signaled the necessity of deliberate rate hikes to bring down inflation. In Europe, ECB Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin reaffirmed the requirement to steer inflation back to 2%. Meanwhile, CrowdStrike is engaged in talks to acquire cybersecurity firm Zscaler in a potentially landmark sector deal.
sections.tech: The tech sector suffered severe losses as Anthropic fell 8.5%, wiping out early gains from its public debut despite underwriters exercising a greenshoe to raise $93.5 billion. Broad market concerns over AI infrastructure spending intensified after Donald Trump threatened taxes on companies building data centers overseas. Nvidia faces leadership transition issues as CFO Colette Kress prepares to steer earnings calls following Jensen Huang's exit amid regulatory scrutiny. Offsetting some gloom, Oracle confirmed its OpenAI infrastructure agreement is fully funded following its final capital raise.
